newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger amid U.S. buying.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger amid U.S. buying.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday, sharply outperforming U.S. Treasuries amid buying by overseas and U.S. investors and some domestic short-covering, analysts said.

"There's some hype in Canada with some shorts getting squeezed out," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with financial analysis firm Technical Data. "We saw good buying out of the U.S. and domestically today."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$2.05 to C$114.60 to yield 6.804 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 31/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 21 basis points from 30 basis points at Monday's close.

"There's a very limited number of places you can look for value in the Canadian yield curve and clearly moving out to the long end is one way you can do it," said Jim Webber, director of fixed income research with TD Securities Inc. "Against a background of a fairly well performing U.S. market, we've just gone absolutely ballistic."
Analysts said expectations of a Bank of Canada rate cut also prompted a rally in the short end of the yield curve. An easing was expected amid recent strength in the dollar.

Canada's dollar closed at its strongest level in more than a year on Tuesday, ending at C$1.3301 (US$0.7518). In making its most recent rate cuts, the Bank of Canada cited the tightening impact of a strengthening currency on monetary conditions in Canada.
Analysts also said bond market fundamentals remain positive in Canada, which is also contributing to further spread narrowing.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$1.15 to C$106.30 to yield 6.150 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 18/32 to yield 6.27 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 12 basis points from three basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 2.89 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.16 percent.
